title: LTX-2: Efficient Joint Audio-Visual Foundation Model
finding: Per authors, LTX-2 is an asymmetric dual-stream transformer (14B video stream + 5B audio stream) with bidirectional audio-video cross-attention, a multilingual text encoder and modality-aware CFG, generating synchronized speech, foley and ambience; claimed SOTA audiovisual quality among open-source systems at a fraction of proprietary compute.
why_for_us: This is the technical report of the model family we run (LTX-2.5 distilled int8); read it for the intended conditioning knobs (modality-CFG, audio stream) before tuning our audio-to-video lip sync and Polish prompts, and to know what the multilingual encoder was designed for.

title: LTX-Video: Realtime Video Latent Diffusion
finding: Per authors, a Video-VAE with 1:192 compression (32x32x8 pixels per token) lets the DiT use full spatiotemporal attention, and the VAE decoder performs the last denoising step; it renders 5 s of 24 fps 768x512 video in 2 s on an H100, with T2V and I2V trained jointly.
why_for_us: Explains why our clip lengths snap to 8k+1 frames (9..97) and resolutions to multiples of 32, and why decoder-side denoising matters when we swap VAEs or tile-decode on the 5090; baseline speed reference for our per-clip cost model.

title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
finding: Per authors, Wan ships 1.3B and 14B DiT models covering up to eight tasks (I2V, instruction editing, personalization); the 14B model beats open and commercial models on their benchmarks, and the 1.3B model needs only 8.19 GB VRAM; all code and weights are open-sourced.
why_for_us: Main alternative/backup to LTX on one 5090: Wan 14B I2V for hero shots where LTX motion fails, Wan 1.3B for cheap drafts; most talking-head and reference-to-video add-ons (VACE, FantasyTalking, InfiniteTalk, Phantom) are built on Wan.

title: HunyuanVideo 1.5 Technical Report
finding: Per authors, an 8.3B-parameter model with selective and sliding tile attention (SSTA), glyph-aware bilingual text encoding and a video super-resolution network reaches open-source SOTA for T2V and I2V while enabling efficient inference on consumer-grade GPUs.
why_for_us: Candidate second engine sized for a single 32 GB card; its separate super-resolution stage is a pattern we could copy (render low-res with LTX, upscale separately). Check licence territory terms before use in the EU.

title: HunyuanVideo: A Systematic Framework For Large Video Generative Models
finding: Per authors, a 13B+ parameter open video model (then the largest open-source one) that, by professional evaluation, outperforms Runway Gen-3, Luma 1.6 and three top Chinese models; code for the base model and applications is released.
why_for_us: Reference architecture behind HunyuanVideo-Avatar and the model most speed-up papers benchmark on (TeaCache, STA, Sparse VideoGen); useful context, but at 13B it is heavier than LTX on our card.

title: CogVideoX: Text-to-Video Diffusion Models with An Expert Transformer
finding: Per authors, a DiT with a 3D causal VAE and expert adaptive LayerNorm generates 10-second, 16 fps, 768x1360 videos; progressive training and multi-resolution frame packing improve long, high-motion clips; VAE, captioner and model weights are public.
why_for_us: Base model for identity-preserving work (ConsisID, Concat-ID); its video captioning pipeline is a template for captioning our own LoRA training clips.

title: SkyReels-V2: Infinite-length Film Generative Model
finding: Per authors, combines an MLLM shot-language captioner (SkyCaptioner-V1), progressive-resolution pretraining, motion-specific RL and a diffusion forcing framework with non-decreasing noise schedules to synthesize long, film-style videos beyond the usual 5-10 s limit; code and models are released.
why_for_us: Relevant if we need shots longer than 97 frames without hard cuts: diffusion-forcing extension is an alternative to chaining clips; the shot-grammar captioner idea can structure our prompts (shot size, camera move, expression).

title: Stable Video Diffusion: Scaling Latent Video Diffusion Models to Large Datasets
finding: Per authors, video LDM training should be split into text-to-image pretraining, video pretraining and high-quality video finetuning, with systematic data curation; the base model gives a strong motion prior for image-to-video and accepts camera-motion-specific LoRA modules.
why_for_us: Foundational evidence that I2V from a strong keyframe plus small camera-motion LoRAs is a sound design, i.e. our stage-1 keyframe then stage-2 animation split.

title: Generative Inbetweening through Frame-wise Conditions-Driven Video Generation
finding: Per authors, FCVG extracts matched lines from the two keyframes and interpolates them frame by frame as explicit per-frame conditions, which markedly improves temporal stability of first/last-frame inbetweening, especially with large motion gaps, for linear and non-linear paths.
why_for_us: Directly addresses our first/last-keyframe shots that morph or wobble: add an explicit per-frame guide (lines, pose or depth interpolated between keyframes) instead of relying on two endpoint latents alone.

title: CameraCtrl: Enabling Camera Control for Text-to-Video Generation
finding: Per authors, a plug-and-play camera-pose control module trained on top of a frozen video diffusion model gives accurate camera trajectories; training videos with diverse camera distributions and appearance similar to the base model improve controllability and generalization.
why_for_us: Real alternative to our camera moves made from crops of one image: a pose-conditioned adapter (or camera LoRAs) yields true parallax instead of 2D zoom/pan; their data finding tells us how to pick clips if we train our own camera LoRA.

title: Recammaster: Camera-Controlled Generative Rendering From a Single Video
finding: Per authors, ReCamMaster re-renders an input video along novel camera trajectories via a simple video-conditioning mechanism on a pretrained T2V model, trained on a multi-camera synchronized Unreal Engine 5 dataset, and substantially outperforms prior methods; also usable for stabilization, super-resolution and outpainting.
why_for_us: Lets us render a static talking-head take once and add a camera move afterwards while keeping the original lip motion; outpainting helps reframe 9:16 vs 16:9 deliverables.

title: VACE: All-in-One Video Creation and Editing
finding: Per authors, a Video Condition Unit packs editing, reference and mask inputs into one interface and a Context Adapter injects them, so one model handles reference-to-video, video-to-video and masked editing at parity with task-specific models.
why_for_us: One Wan-based model for multi-keyframe placement, masked fixes (re-render only a bad mouth or hand region) and reference-driven shots; reduces the number of specialised ComfyUI workflows we maintain.

title: Phantom: Subject-Consistent Video Generation via Cross-Modal Alignment
finding: Per authors, Phantom redesigns joint text-image injection and trains on text-image-video triplets for single- and multi-subject reference-to-video, reducing image content leakage and multi-subject confusion, and outperforms closed commercial solutions, with emphasis on human ID preservation.
why_for_us: Reference-to-video route to keep our presenter identical across shots without per-person LoRA training; content leakage (background or pose copied from the reference) is exactly the failure to test for.

title: Concat-ID: Towards Universal Identity-Preserving Video Synthesis
finding: Per authors, reference face features from the VAE are concatenated with video latents along the sequence dimension and handled by the existing 3D self-attention only, with no extra modules; cross-video pairing and multi-stage training balance identity consistency against facial editability.
why_for_us: Cheapest identity mechanism to replicate on a full-attention DiT like LTX (append reference latent tokens, no new weights); the identity-vs-editability trade-off warns that a strong ID lock can freeze expressions in talking shots.

title: Long Context Tuning for Video Generation
finding: Per authors, LCT extends full attention from one shot to all shots of a scene with interleaved 3D position embeddings and asynchronous noise, enabling joint or autoregressive multi-shot generation with no extra parameters; with context-causal finetuning it supports KV-cached shot extension.
why_for_us: Blueprint for multi-shot consistency (same person, lighting and set across a cut) instead of generating each shot independently from separately made keyframes.

title: HoloCine: Holistic Generation of Cinematic Multi-Shot Long Video Narratives
finding: Per authors, HoloCine generates whole scenes at once using Window Cross-Attention to tie prompts to specific shots and Sparse Inter-Shot Self-Attention (dense within, sparse between shots) for minute-scale efficiency, showing persistent memory for characters and scenes.
why_for_us: Shows per-shot prompting inside one generation, which maps onto our shot lists; minute-scale scenes likely exceed one 5090, so mostly a design reference.

title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
finding: Per authors, decoupled cross-attention for image features gives a 22M-parameter adapter that matches or beats fully fine-tuned image-prompt models, transfers to custom models from the same base and to structural controls, and combines with text prompts.
why_for_us: Standard way to keep the same face and outfit across all stage-1 keyframes before they reach LTX; identity consistency in keyframes is cheaper than fixing it in video.

title: OmniHuman-1: Rethinking the Scaling-Up of One-Stage Conditioned Human Animation Models
finding: Per authors, a DiT trained with mixed motion-related conditions (audio, pose/video) scales data for human animation, supporting face close-up to full-body, talking and singing, human-object interaction and multiple driving modalities, more realistically than prior end-to-end audio-driven methods.
why_for_us: Quality target for talking-body shots; the abstract does not state a weights release, so use its mixed-condition idea (audio + pose) to choose open alternatives rather than as a tool.

title: FantasyTalking: Realistic Talking Portrait Generation via Coherent Motion Synthesis
finding: Per authors, built on a pretrained video DiT, it uses clip-level audio-visual alignment for global motion, then frame-level lip refinement with a lip-tracing mask, a lightweight cross-attention identity module instead of a reference network, and a motion-intensity module controlling facial keypoints and body joints; demo, code and models are released.
why_for_us: Open Wan-based talking-portrait option; lip-tracing-mask refinement and motion-intensity control are what our Polish talking heads need (natural head and body motion, not only lips).

title: InfiniteTalk: Audio-driven Video Generation for Sparse-Frame Video Dubbing
finding: Per authors, sparse-frame video dubbing keeps reference keyframes for identity, gestures and camera path while regenerating audio-synchronized full-body motion; a streaming generator with temporal context frames gives seamless chunk transitions for unlimited-length dubbing, SOTA on HDTF, CelebV-HQ and EMTD.
why_for_us: Fits re-voicing existing clips into Polish: keep the original take's keyframes and camera, regenerate face and body to the new audio, and chain chunks beyond 97 frames without seams.

title: Hallo3: Highly Dynamic and Realistic Portrait Image Animation with Video Diffusion Transformer
finding: Per authors, the first use of a pretrained transformer video model for portrait animation, with an identity reference network (causal 3D VAE + stacked transformer layers) and studied speech-audio conditioning plus motion frames for continuous audio-driven video; handles non-frontal views and dynamic backgrounds better than U-Net methods.
why_for_us: Recipe for the two things our talking heads struggle with: identity drift over long takes (reference network) and continuity across chunks (motion frames).

title: LatentSync: Taming Audio-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Models for Lip Sync with SyncNet Supervision
finding: Per authors, audio-conditioned LDMs learn visual-visual shortcuts and neglect audio, which SyncNet supervision fixes; their StableSyncNet raises SyncNet accuracy from 91% to 94% on HDTF, and TREPA improves temporal consistency, beating prior lip-sync methods on HDTF and VoxCeleb2.
why_for_us: Post-pass lip-sync fixer for clips where LTX audio-to-video drifts (mouth region only); SyncNet confidence is a cheap automatic QC score for every rendered Polish clip.

title: MuseTalk: Real-Time High-Fidelity Video Dubbing via Spatio-Temporal Sampling
finding: Per authors, latent-space audio-visual fusion with Informative Frame Sampling and Dynamic Margin Sampling delivers 30 FPS at 256x256 on an NVIDIA V100, with better visual fidelity than SOTA and comparable lip-sync accuracy; code is public.
why_for_us: Very cheap mouth-only dubbing fallback for low-stakes Polish variants; the 256x256 face crop limits use on close-ups.

title: HunyuanVideo-Avatar: High-Fidelity Audio-Driven Human Animation for Multiple Characters
finding: Per authors, an MM-DiT with a character image injection module (removing train/inference condition mismatch), an Audio Emotion Module transferring emotion from a reference image, and a Face-Aware Audio Adapter using face masks so separate audio drives separate characters.
why_for_us: Only needed for two-person dialogue shots; face-mask audio routing and an emotion reference image are the transferable ideas even if we stay on LTX.

title: MultiTalk: Enhancing 3D Talking Head Generation Across Languages with Multilingual Video Dataset
finding: Per authors, lip-sync accuracy degrades for languages poorly covered by training data; a 420+ hour talking-video dataset in 20 languages plus language-specific style embeddings significantly improves multilingual 3D talking-head performance, and they propose a multilingual lip-sync metric.
why_for_us: The only direct evidence here that lip sync is language-dependent: build a small Polish test set (sz/cz/rz, nasal vowels) and measure sync per language instead of trusting English benchmarks.

title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
finding: Per authors, rectified flow with noise sampling biased toward perceptually relevant scales beats standard diffusion formulations, and an MM-DiT with separate text/image weights improves text comprehension, typography and human preference, following predictable scaling trends.
why_for_us: Architectural basis of SD3 and FLUX-style keyframe models; explains why they handle on-image text (Polish signage, captions) better than SDXL.

title: FLUX.1 Kontext: Flow Matching for In-Context Image Generation and Editing in Latent Space
finding: Per authors, simple sequence concatenation unifies generation and editing; it preserves objects and characters better across multiple editing turns than other editing models, is significantly faster, and is evaluated on KontextBench with 1026 image-prompt pairs over five task categories.
why_for_us: Best fit for making first/last keyframes from one master image (change expression, pose, background, framing while keeping the person) to feed LTX keyframe conditioning; verify the open-weights licence before commercial use.

title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
finding: Per authors, a three times larger UNet with a second text encoder, new conditioning schemes, multi-aspect-ratio training and a refinement model give drastically better results than earlier Stable Diffusion, competitive with black-box generators; code and weights are released.
why_for_us: Light keyframe fallback with the largest ecosystem of LoRAs, IP-Adapter and ControlNets, for when FLUX VRAM or licence is a constraint.

title: InstructPix2Pix: Learning to Follow Image Editing Instructions
finding: Per authors, a conditional diffusion model trained on a GPT-3 + Stable Diffusion generated dataset edits real images from written instructions in a single forward pass, in seconds, without per-example fine-tuning or inversion.
why_for_us: Origin of instruction-based keyframe editing; mainly background, plus a synthetic-pair data recipe if we ever train our own edit LoRA for presenter variants.

title: Timestep Embedding Tells: It's Time to Cache for Video Diffusion Model
finding: Per authors, TeaCache is training-free: it estimates output change from timestep-modulated inputs and reuses cached outputs when change is small, giving up to 4.41x acceleration over Open-Sora-Plan with -0.07% VBench degradation.
why_for_us: Gain comes from skipping steps, so on our already distilled few-step LTX expect little; it matters for Wan/Hunyuan fallbacks and non-distilled hero renders. Test on a fixed seed set before enabling.

title: Fast Video Generation with Sliding Tile Attention
finding: Per authors, attention takes 800 of 945 s for a 5 s 720p HunyuanVideo clip; tile-wise sliding-window attention is 2.8-17x faster than FlashAttention-2 and 1.6-10x faster than FA3, cutting end-to-end latency from 945 s to 685 s training-free, or 268 s with finetuning at a 0.09% VBench drop.
why_for_us: Quantifies that attention dominates cost at higher resolution and length; if we move to 720p or past 97 frames, sparse/tiled attention is the first lever before buying more GPU time.

title: Sparse VideoGen: Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers with Spatial-Temporal Sparsity
finding: Per authors, attention heads split into spatial and temporal heads with distinct sparse patterns; online profiling plus custom kernels gives training-free 2.28x and 2.33x end-to-end speedups on CogVideoX-v1.5 and HunyuanVideo while preserving quality.
why_for_us: Training-free speed-up candidate for full-attention DiTs like LTX; needs a kernel port, so a medium-effort experiment after SageAttention.

title: SageAttention: Accurate 8-Bit Attention for Plug-and-play Inference Acceleration
finding: Per authors, 8-bit quantized attention reaches about 2.1x the OPS of FlashAttention2 and 2.7x of xformers, with better accuracy than FlashAttention3 and almost no end-to-end metric loss across language, image and video generation models.
why_for_us: Lowest-effort speed-up for our ComfyUI stack, complementary to int8 weights; benchmark on the 5090 with a fixed seed set and check lip-sync QC does not regress.

title: SVDQuant: Absorbing Outliers by Low-Rank Components for 4-Bit Diffusion Models
finding: Per authors, 4-bit weights and activations with a low-rank SVD branch absorbing outliers plus the fused Nunchaku engine cut 12B FLUX.1 memory by 3.5x, give 3.0x speedup over W4A16 on a 16 GB laptop 4090 (INT4) and 3.1x over W4A16 on an RTX 5090 with NVFP4; LoRAs work without re-quantization.
why_for_us: Measured on our GPU class (RTX 5090, NVFP4): run the FLUX keyframe stage in 4-bit so keyframe and LTX models can share the 32 GB card without reloading.

title: Self Forcing: Bridging the Train-Test Gap in Autoregressive Video Diffusion
finding: Per authors, training autoregressive video diffusion on its own rollouts with KV caching, a video-level loss, few-step diffusion and stochastic gradient truncation removes exposure bias; with a rolling KV cache it reaches real-time streaming generation with sub-second latency on a single GPU, matching slower non-causal models.
why_for_us: Path to long or streaming talking-head takes on one GPU without quality decay across chunks; relevant once we need takes longer than 97 frames.
